target_customer: Defense, commodities trading and disaster response users who need continuous Earth observation imagery through clouds and darkness
problem: Optical satellites are blocked by weather and night, while radar (SAR) imagery is hard for humans and standard vision pipelines to use. The company translates SAR backscatter into analysis-ready optical imagery in near real time.
business_model: Foundation model and imagery API, pricing not public
product_category: Earth observation foundation models (SAR to optical translation)

founders.name: Dhenenjay Yadav
education: Listed as Ex-IIMA on the YC page
founders.background_notes: YC page lists computer vision, RL, UAV building and past esports experience.

founders.name: Atharva Peshkar
founders.background_notes: Some aggregators list Peshkar as CEO; the YC page lists Yadav as CEO.

technical_complexity.rationale: Training a one step diffusion model that converts radar backscatter to photorealistic optical imagery requires research level ML and large satellite datasets. Academic work on SAR to RGB translation existed, per search results.

defensibility.rationale: Model quality claims are self reported (FID 30.24) and unverified by independent review. Academic methods are public and large EO players have foundation model efforts.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: An independent YC tier list review rated competition medium and said these players have EO foundation model efforts; no incumbent product doing the same translation was confirmed.

market_need_then: Weather and darkness limit optical imagery, per the company page, and SAR demand is growing among defense and commodities buyers. No dated customer evidence was found.

branding.domain_note: Company uses axionorbital.space rather than a .com. Easily confused with Axiom Space in search results.

identity.logo: Logo image on the site; no description found

branding.brand_signature: ORION, the flagship SAR to optical model

brand_strength.rationale: Little press beyond YC aggregators and one Turkish startup article. Search for the name returns Axiom Space news instead.

outcome_analysis: AxionOrbital Space is an Active Winter 2026 YC company with two technical founders and a launched model called ORION in January 2026. No verified funding, customers or independent benchmark were found, so no outcome can be judged. Key risks are unproven demand and large EO players with foundation model efforts.
notes: Unverified funding figures from aggregators only: a $100K seed (Signalbase headline), about $500K (Yespress) and $600K total (Standout), with no named investors and one aggregator naming the co-founder as investor. None recorded as rounds. The company site fetch returned only a title and logo. Competitor list left empty because the competitor sources found were undated; the YC tier list review named Google, Airbus and Planet as EO foundation model efforts. UPDATE (completeness pass): a $100K seed is recorded from a single outlet (Signalbase), with no date or investors given. Standout reports $600K total raised and Yespress about $500K, which conflict and are not summed; the gap is known.
